title: CastillosCVEP40
description: A code-modulated Visual Evoked Potential (c-VEP) electroencephalography dataset from 12 healthy participants investigating burst c-VEP as a reactive brain-computer interface paradigm. The study employed a factorial design manipulating stimulus pattern (burst versus m-sequence) and amplitude depth (100% versus 40% modulation) to optimize classification accuracy while improving user visual comfort. This dataset contains the m-sequence c-VEP subset at 40% amplitude depth modulation (60 trials per subject). Data were acquired at 500 Hz using 32-channel EEG with convolutional neural network-based classification achieving up to 95.6% accuracy in the full factorial study.
methods_description: EEG data acquired from 12 healthy participants (mean age 30.6±7.1 years, 4 female, 8 male) using a BrainProducts LiveAmp 32-channel system at 500 Hz sampling rate with active Acticap electrodes referenced to FCz. Participants completed a reactive BCI task with four visual targets presented on a Dell monitor (60 Hz, 1920×1080 pixels, 265 cd/m²). Each trial consisted of a 0.5-second visual cue (red-bordered square) followed by 2.2 seconds of aperiodic visual stimulation at 40% amplitude depth modulation (m-sequence code type). The dataset contains 60 trials per subject (15 blocks × 4 trials per block). Preprocessing included average re-referencing, IIR notch filtering (49.9-50.1 Hz, order 16), and baseline removal. Classification employed convolutional neural networks with sliding window feature extraction and bitwise decoding.
